assessment: Study relationships rather than the organizer as a whole. Neither combined timing nor customer reports establish a cause. These alternatives retain existing parts, dimensions, assortment, reversible joints, accepted counts and colors, and delivery commitments; their benefit and resource fit need testing.

openings.claim: A missing explicit relation between each supplied partition and its destination may explain some reported errors and short-partition confusion.
openings.delta: Represent the ordered layout as partition-to-slot relations. Replace the generic three-layout diagram with an order-specific silhouette showing each partition's length, orientation and destination. Recompose by matching every required partition to a depicted destination, counting repeated shapes separately; use that same mapping for packing and customer placement without changing the parts.
openings.prediction: With contents independently verified complete, the specific diagram reduces short-partition placement errors relative to the current diagram. Unchanged errors would weaken the mapping explanation.
openings.probe: Randomly split the ten participants between diagrams, balancing layouts. Use five of the 15 sample organizers and reset between participants. Record correct unaided arrangement, short-partition errors and completion time. Treat this as screening, not proof of the pilot target; time workshop checking and cost the replacement diagram.
assumptions: A readable diagram can distinguish the relevant destinations.
Replacement printing and preparation fit both cost caps and the fixed schedule.

openings.claim: Relations between consecutive orders may contribute more delay than any individual organizer configuration: switching layouts could increase selection or checking time.
openings.delta: Represent production as order-to-order transitions. Recompose into the same accepted orders by sequencing equal layouts together, keeping an individual count-and-color slip attached throughout. Assembly and packing remain complete for every order.
openings.prediction: Switching layout increases selection or checking time for the same target layout; an insertion-only difference would favor layout difficulty over transition cost.
openings.probe: Use ten remaining samples in five same-target pairs, one following the same layout and one following a different layout. Counterbalance worker and sequence; hold target color constant. Separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing, and audit contents before considering resequencing.
assumptions: Testing fits available working time before the unchanged delivery date.
Per-order slips remain attached so batching does not substitute colors or compartment counts.
